//: Claude Code Manager - recommended VS Code terminal settings (BUILD 2026-07-09 22:31 v12 panel-top).
//1: Merge these keys into your VS Code user settings.json. install.ps1 can do it for you (with a backup).
//tabs: Show a vertical tab list on the LEFT side of the terminal panel - it never shrinks like horizontal tabs.
//title: Use the title the shell/hooks set via escape sequence -> '<model> <status> <folder>'.
terminal.integrated.tabs.title: ${sequence}
//active: Make the selected terminal unmistakable. `terminal.tab.activeBorder` is the ONLY terminal-tab-specific colour VS Code has, and it is a thin line - the row's fill comes from the GLOBAL list colours below, which also tint the Explorer/Search selection. That is the trade.
//active2: inactiveSelection* is the one that matters: while you type in the terminal, the tab list is unfocused, so the selected row is drawn as an *inactive* selection.
//active3: The blue fill tracks the list SELECTION, which VS Code clears when you click the empty area below the tabs. The 1px `is-active` bar is the only marker tied to the actually-active terminal, so it is bright red - it is what survives.
//bell: A terminal that receives BEL gets a timed status icon on ITS OWN tab: statusList.add({id:'bell',severity:Warning,icon:bell}, bellDuration). list.warningForeground paints that icon.
//focus: One click on a tab puts the caret on that session's prompt line. Default is doubleClick.
//persist: Keep terminals across window reloads so the hub survives a restart.
//panel: Put the terminal panel at the TOP. This only applies to a workspace with no stored panel position: VS Code persists `workbench.panel.position` PER WORKSPACE (0=left 1=right 2=bottom 3=top). The ccm-hub extension converts the workspaces that already have one, once each.
